Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/plugins/cache/mattpocock/mattpocock-skills/1.3.2/skills/productivity/writing-for-agents

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

#!/bin/bash
# Weekly CFB Victory Model freeze - all 16 Big 12 teams, then the comparison.
#
# Run it Wednesday of a game week. A Chrome window opens; that is required, not
# a bug. Headless breaks the Power BI team slicer.
#
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh                       # all Big 12, 2026
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU    # just these two
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --year 2027
#
# Snapshots land in data/weekly_snapshots/ and are copied to
# ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/ along with each team's comparison text.
set -euo pipefail

# Background/launchd shells get a minimal PATH, so nothing here relies on it.
UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Without this, Python block-buffers stdout whenever the run is redirected to a
# file, so a 10-minute run shows nothing until it finishes.
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Capture exits non-zero if any team failed both passes. Skip the comparison
# then: it diffs whatever snapshots are newest, so after a failed capture it
# prints last week's numbers as if they were today's. Captures are idempotent,
# so fix the cause and re-run (or --teams <the failed ones>).
echo "=== capture ==="
rc=0
"$UV" run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py "$@" || rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "=== comparison SKIPPED: capture failed (exit $rc) ==="
    echo "Fix the error above and re-run. Nothing was compared or archived."
    exit "$rc"
fi

echo
echo "=== comparison ==="
"$UV" run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive

# Opening lines for the coming games. cfbd_pull.py skips files that exist, so
# move last week's file aside and put it back if the pull fails. A failure here
# never fails the run: the capture above is the part that cannot be redone.
echo
echo "=== model vs opening line ==="
LINES=data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv
[ -f "$LINES" ] && mv "$LINES" "$LINES.prev"
if "$UV" run python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$LINES" ]; then
    rm -f "$LINES.prev"
    "$UV" run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py || echo "market view failed"
else
    [ -f "$LINES.prev" ] && mv "$LINES.prev" "$LINES"
    echo "CFBD line pull failed; skipped. The capture and comparison above are fine."
fi

exit $rc

`/forecast-capture` skill, which snapshots predictions **before kickoff** and reports what
moved since the prior week.

## Scope and entry point (changed 2026-09-02, per Eric)

- **All 16 Big 12 teams every week**, not Baylor only. The list is the `BIG12` constant in
  `weekly_capture.py` — one home; do not copy team lists into the wrapper or the skill.
  `--teams`/`--team` still narrow a run. Budget ~10 min for the full sweep.
- **One entry point:** `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh` (capture → compare
  `--all --archive`). It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path.

  `CFB_Victory_Model/data/`. Registered in `backup-manifest.json` as `personal`/ssd —

#!/bin/bash
# Weekly CFB Victory Model freeze - all 16 Big 12 teams, then the comparison.
#
# Run it Wednesday of a game week. A Chrome window opens; that is required, not
# a bug. Headless breaks the Power BI team slicer.
#
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh                       # all Big 12, 2026
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU    # just these two
#   scripts/weekly_run.sh --year 2027
#
# Snapshots land in data/weekly_snapshots/ and are copied to
# ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/ along with each team's comparison text.
set -euo pipefail

# Background/launchd shells get a minimal PATH, so nothing here relies on it.
UV=/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# Without this, Python block-buffers stdout whenever the run is redirected to a
# file, so a 10-minute run shows nothing until it finishes.
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Capture exits non-zero if any team failed both passes. Skip the comparison
# then: it diffs whatever snapshots are newest, so after a failed capture it
# prints last week's numbers as if they were today's. Captures are idempotent,
# so fix the cause and re-run (or --teams <the failed ones>).
echo "=== capture ==="
rc=0
"$UV" run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py "$@" || rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo
    echo "=== comparison SKIPPED: capture failed (exit $rc) ==="
    echo "Fix the error above and re-run. Nothing was compared or archived."
    exit "$rc"
fi

echo
echo "=== comparison ==="
"$UV" run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive

# Opening lines for the coming games. cfbd_pull.py skips files that exist, so
# move last week's file aside and put it back if the pull fails. A failure here
# never fails the run: the capture above is the part that cannot be redone.
echo
echo "=== model vs opening line ==="
LINES=data/cfbd/lines_2026_regular.csv
[ -f "$LINES" ] && mv "$LINES" "$LINES.prev"
if "$UV" run python cfbd_pull.py --years 2026 --only lines >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$LINES" ]; then
    rm -f "$LINES.prev"
    "$UV" run --with pandas --with scipy --with tabulate python market_view.py || echo "market view failed"
else
    [ -f "$LINES.prev" ] && mv "$LINES.prev" "$LINES"
    echo "CFBD line pull failed; skipped. The capture and comparison above are fine."
fi

exit $rc

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Weekly capture of CFB Victory Model forecasts, before the games are played.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
The report's "Chance of Victory" column is overwritten with the realised result
once a game finishes. Across 2019-2025 that destroyed every pre-game probability
the model ever produced - no Brier score, no calibration curve, ever. This script
freezes the forecast each week so 2026 becomes the first gradable season.

HOW IT WORKS
------------
Loads the published Power BI report as a normal browser would, sets the Team and
Year slicers, and reads the rendered table. No API replay, no header spoofing -
it is exactly what a visitor's browser does, which is what the report was
published for. One report session per run.

USAGE
-----
  python weekly_capture.py                     # default: all 16 Big 12 teams, 2026
  python weekly_capture.py --team Baylor       # one team
  python weekly_capture.py --teams Baylor TCU "Iowa State"
  python weekly_capture.py --no-archive        # skip the DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive copy

Output: data/weekly_snapshots/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<team>.csv  (one file per run)
        data/weekly_forecast_log.csv                   (append-only, all runs)
        ../CFB_Forecast_Archive/<year>/<date>_<team>.csv   (read-only copy)

Idempotent per day: re-running for the same team+date overwrites that snapshot
and de-duplicates the log, so a retry after a failure is safe.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, csv, datetime as dt, shutil, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright, TimeoutError as PWTimeout

# The site moved to a new report around 2026-10-05; the old one still loads but froze.
# If captures stop changing week to week, compare this key with the iframe on
# https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/.
REPORT = ("https://app.powerbi.com/view?r=eyJrIjoiZjI0OWJlYTMtOGQ4YS00NTIzLTllZWItY2Uy"
          "ZGY4OTEyNTUzIiwidCI6ImJkOWFiODAzLTFhNWMtNDM2MC04OGM2LWZlNGJiNDZkMGRkZCJ9"
          "&pageName=fe8c0d478504c7c16beb")
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SNAP = ROOT / "data" / "weekly_snapshots"
LOG  = ROOT / "data" / "weekly_forecast_log.csv"

# Read-only mirror of each snapshot, one folder per season. The canonical data
# stays under data/ - this exists so the freezes can be browsed and backed up
# without opening the model repo.
ARCHIVE = ROOT.parent / "CFB_Forecast_Archive"

# Big 12, 2026 membership (16). Spelled the way the report's Team slicer spells
# them - "Iowa State" not "Iowa St.", "UCF" not "Central Florida". A wrong name
# fails loudly with `never appeared (saw [...])`, it never silently captures the
# wrong team.
BIG12 = ["Arizona", "Arizona State", "Baylor", "BYU", "Cincinnati", "Colorado",
         "Houston", "Iowa State", "Kansas", "Kansas State", "Oklahoma State",
         "TCU", "Texas Tech", "UCF", "Utah", "West Virginia"]

FIELDS = ["captured_at","season","team","week","game_id","opponent","opp_plus_minus",
          "opp_model_rank","venue","exp_pts","opp_exp_pts","win_prob","opp_win_prob",
          "actual_pts","opp_actual_pts"]

# Paste CONFERENCES here:
CONFERENCES = {
    "Big 12": [
        "Arizona", "Arizona State", "Baylor", "BYU", "Cincinnati",
        "Colorado", "Houston", "Iowa State", "Kansas", "Kansas State",
.....

    for _ in range(10):                    # state read can lag the close
        if page.evaluate(JS_STATE).get(title) == value:
            break
        page.wait_for_timeout(600)
    if verbose:
        print(f"    set {title} = {value}")


def capture(page, team: str, year: str, verbose=True) -> list[dict]:
    set_slicer(page, "Year", str(year), verbose)
    set_slicer(page, "Team", team, verbose)

    page.wait_for_timeout(2500)
    d = page.evaluate(JS_READ)
    if not d.get("ok"):
        raise RuntimeError(d.get("err"))

    state = d["slicers"]
    if state.get("Team") != team or state.get("Year") != str(year):
        raise RuntimeError(f"slicer state wrong after set: {state}")

    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    rows = []
    for r in d["games"]:
        # r: [SelectRow, Game#, WK, Opponent, Opp+/-, OppRank, blank, H/A,
        #     ExpPts, OppExpPts, ActPts, OppActPts, Win%, OppWin%]
        if len(r) < 14 or not r[3] or not r[2]:
            continue                                   # skip the totals row
        try:
            wk = int(float(r[2]))
            gid = int(float(r[1]))
        except ValueError:
            continue
        pct = lambda s: round(float(s.rstrip('%'))/100, 4) if s.endswith('%') else None
        num = lambda s: (int(float(s)) if s not in ("", None) else None)
        rows.append(dict(captured_at=today, season=year, team=team, week=wk, game_id=gid,
                         opponent=r[3], opp_plus_minus=r[4], opp_model_rank=r[5],
                         venue=r[7], exp_pts=num(r[8]), opp_exp_pts=num(r[9]),
                         win_prob=pct(r[12]), opp_win_prob=pct(r[13]),
                         actual_pts=num(r[10]), opp_actual_pts=num(r[11])))
    return rows


def slugify(team: str) -> str:
    return team.lower().replace(" ", "-").replace("&", "and").replace("'", "")


def write_out(rows: list[dict], team: str, archive: bool = True):
    SNAP.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    today = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    slug = slugify(team)
    dest = SNAP / f"{today}_{slug}.csv"
    with dest.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=FIELDS); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)

    existing = []
    if LOG.exists():
        existing = [r for r in csv.DictReader(LOG.open(encoding="utf-8"))
                    if not (r.get("captured_at") == today and r.get("team") == team)]
    with LOG.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=FIELDS); w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(existing); w.writerows(rows)

    if archive:
        season = rows[0].get("season") or str(dt.date.today().year)
        adir = ARCHIVE / str(season)
        adir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(dest, adir / dest.name)

    return dest, len(existing) + len(rows)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--teams", nargs="+", default=BIG12,
                    help="teams to capture (default: all 16 Big 12)")
    ap.add_argument("--team", help="single team (shorthand for --teams X)")
    ap.add_argument("--conference", help="conference name (e.g. Big 12 )")
    ap.add_argument("--year", default="2026")
    ap.add_argument("--no-archive", action="store_true",
                    help=f"do not copy snapshots into {ARCHIVE}")
    ap.add_argument("--headless", action="store_true",
                    help="not recommended - Power BI's virtual slicer list does "
                         "not populate without a compositor, so team selection fails")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    # 2. REPLACE 'teams = [a.team] if a.team else a.teams' WITH THIS BLOCK:
    if a.conference:
        if a.conference not in CONFERENCES:
            print(f"Unknown conference '{a.conference}'. Available: {', '.join(CONFERENCES.keys())}")
            sys.exit(1)
        teams = CONFERENCES[a.conference]
    elif a.team:
        teams = [a.team]
    else:
        teams = a.teams

    fails = []
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        # MUST run headed. In headless Chromium the slicer's virtualised option
        # list never renders past the first ~8 alphabetical entries, so any team
        # after "Arizona State" is unreachable. Verified: headless fails on
        # Baylor, headed succeeds. Scheduled runs need an interactive session
        # (or a virtual display).
        b = p.chromium.launch(headless=a.headless)
        pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1600, "height": 1000})
        print(f"loading report ...")
        pg.goto(REPORT, wait_until="load", timeout=90_000)
        pg.wait_for_timeout(9000)

        def run(team_list):
            """Capture each team, returning the ones that did not produce rows."""
            missed = []
            for t in team_list:
                print(f"\n  {t} {a.year}")
                try:
                    rows = capture(pg, t, a.year)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"    FAILED: {e}"); missed.append(t); continue
                if not rows:
                    print(f"    FAILED: no rows"); missed.append(t); continue
                dest, total = write_out(rows, t, archive=not a.no_archive)
                unplayed = sum(1 for r in rows if r["actual_pts"] is None)
                print(f"    {len(rows)} games ({unplayed} still unplayed) -> {dest.name}")
                print(f"    log now {total} rows")
            return missed

        fails = run(teams)

        # One retry round. Over 16 teams a stale dropdown or a slow re-render
        # takes out one or two, and they almost always succeed on a second pass
        # once the app has settled. A name that is genuinely wrong fails twice.
        if fails:
            print(f"\n--- retrying {len(fails)} failed team(s): {', '.join(fails)}")
            fails = run(fails)

        b.close()

    if fails:
        print(f"\nFAILED for: {', '.join(fails)}"); sys.exit(1)
    print(f"\nDone. Log: {LOG}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Compare the two most recent forecast captures and report what moved.

A bare capture tells you nothing about whether the model changed its mind.
This does: which games shifted, which got played, and how the season outlook
drifted. Run straight after weekly_capture.py.

  python compare_snapshots.py                 # Baylor
  python compare_snapshots.py --team TCU
  python compare_snapshots.py --all           # every team captured on the newest date
  python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive # ...and write the text into the archive
  python compare_snapshots.py --list          # show all captures on file
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, csv, datetime as dt, sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SNAP = ROOT / "data" / "weekly_snapshots"
ARCHIVE = ROOT.parent / "CFB_Forecast_Archive"


def slugify(team: str) -> str:
    return team.lower().replace(" ", "-").replace("&", "and").replace("'", "")


def load(team: str):
    """Return [(date, rows)] for one team, oldest first."""
    slug = slugify(team)
        return None


def summarise(rows):
    exp_w = sum(num(r["win_prob"]) or 0 for r in rows)
    raw_w = sum(1 for r in rows
                if num(r["exp_pts"]) is not None
                and num(r["exp_pts"]) > num(r["opp_exp_pts"]))
    played = [r for r in rows if r.get("actual_pts") not in ("", None)]
    return exp_w, raw_w, len(rows), played


def report(team: str):
    """Build the comparison text for one team.

    Returns (lines, stats) or None when the team has no captures. Text is
    returned rather than printed so the same output can go to the terminal and
    into the archive without running the comparison twice.
    """
    caps = load(team)
    if not caps:
        return None

    out: list[str] = []
    date, rows = caps[-1]
    exp_w, raw_w, n, played = summarise(rows)
    stats = dict(team=team, date=date, games=n, exp_wins=exp_w, raw_wins=raw_w,
                 played=len(played), d_exp_wins=0.0, moved=0, newly_played=0,
                 season=rows[0].get("season", ""))

    out.append(f"CAPTURE {date} - {team}")
    out.append(f"  games            : {n}")
    out.append(f"  expected wins    : {exp_w:.2f}   (raw {raw_w}-{n-raw_w})")
    out.append(f"  games played     : {len(played)}")

    age = (dt.date.today() - dt.date.fromisoformat(date)).days
    if age > 0:
        out.append(f"  NOTE: newest capture is {age} day(s) old")

    if len(caps) < 2:
        out.append("")
        out.append("  First capture on file - nothing to compare against yet.")
        return out, stats

    pdate, prev = caps[-2]
    pmap = {r["opponent"]: r for r in prev}
    out.append("")
    out.append(f"CHANGES SINCE {pdate}")

    moved, newly_played = [], []
    for r in rows:
        p = pmap.get(r["opponent"])
        if not p:
            out.append(f"  + NEW GAME: wk{r['week']} {r['opponent']}")
            continue
        if p.get("actual_pts") in ("", None) and r.get("actual_pts") not in ("", None):
            newly_played.append((r, p))
            continue
        d_exp = (num(r["exp_pts"]) or 0) - (num(p["exp_pts"]) or 0)
        d_opp = (num(r["opp_exp_pts"]) or 0) - (num(p["opp_exp_pts"]) or 0)
        d_wp = (num(r["win_prob"]) or 0) - (num(p["win_prob"]) or 0)
        if abs(d_exp) >= 1 or abs(d_opp) >= 1 or abs(d_wp) >= 0.02:
            moved.append((r, d_exp, d_opp, d_wp))

    if newly_played:
        out.append("")
        out.append("  GAMES PLAYED SINCE LAST CAPTURE (forecast now gradable):")
        for r, p in newly_played:
            pm = (num(p["exp_pts"]) or 0) - (num(p["opp_exp_pts"]) or 0)
            am = (num(r["actual_pts"]) or 0) - (num(r["opp_actual_pts"]) or 0)
            hit = "correct" if (pm > 0) == (am > 0) else "WRONG"
            out.append(f"    wk{r['week']:>2} {r['opponent']:<20} "
                       f"forecast {p['exp_pts']}-{p['opp_exp_pts']} ({p['win_prob']}) "
                       f"-> actual {r['actual_pts']}-{r['opp_actual_pts']}  "
                       f"side {hit}, margin miss {abs(pm-am):.0f}")

    if moved:
        out.append("")
        out.append(f"  FORECAST MOVED ({len(moved)} game(s)):")
        for r, de, do, dw in sorted(moved, key=lambda x: -abs(x[3])):
            out.append(f"    wk{r['week']:>2} {r['opponent']:<20} "
                       f"pts {de:+.0f}/{do:+.0f}   win prob {dw*100:+.0f} pts "
                       f"-> now {float(r['win_prob'])*100:.0f}%")
    elif not newly_played:
        out.append("  No material change (no game moved >=1 pt or >=2% win probability).")

    pexp_w, praw_w, _, _ = summarise(prev)
    d_exp_w = exp_w - pexp_w
    out.append("")
    out.append(f"  season expected wins: {pexp_w:.2f} -> {exp_w:.2f}  ({d_exp_w:+.2f})")
    if raw_w != praw_w:
        out.append(f"  raw projection changed: {praw_w}-{len(prev)-praw_w} "
                   f"-> {raw_w}-{n-raw_w}")

    stats.update(d_exp_wins=d_exp_w, moved=len(moved), newly_played=len(newly_played))
    return out, stats


def archive_report(lines: list[str], stats: dict):
    season = stats.get("season") or str(dt.date.today().year)
    adir = ARCHIVE / str(season)
    adir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest = adir / f"{stats['date']}_{slugify(stats['team'])}_compare.txt"
    dest.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return dest


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--team", default="Baylor")
    ap.add_argument("--teams", nargs="+", help="several teams at once")
    ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                    help="every team captured on the newest capture date")
    ap.add_argument("--list", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--archive", action="store_true",
                    help=f"also write each report into {ARCHIVE}/<season>/")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    if a.list:
        for d, r in load(a.team):
            print(f"  {d}  {len(r):>2} games")
        return

    if a.all:
        date = latest_capture_date()
        if not date:
            print(f"No captures found in {SNAP}")
            sys.exit(1)
        teams = teams_captured_on(date)
    elif a.teams:
        teams = a.teams
    else:
        teams = [a.team]

    results, missing = [], []
    for t in teams:
        r = report(t)
        if r is None:
            missing.append(t)
        else:
            results.append(r)

    if not results:
        print(f"No captures found for {', '.join(missing)} in {SNAP}")
        sys.exit(1)

    written = []
    if a.archive:
        written = [archive_report(lines, stats) for lines, stats in results]

    # One team: the full report is the whole point. Many teams: sixteen full
    # blocks is unreadable, so lead with a rollup and expand only the teams
    # where something actually happened.
    if len(results) == 1:
        print("\n".join(results[0][0]))
    else:
        print(f"ROLLUP - {len(results)} team(s), capture {results[0][1]['date']}")
        print(f"  {'team':<16} {'exp wins':>8} {'change':>7} {'played':>6} {'moved':>6}")
        for _, s in sorted(results, key=lambda x: -x[1]["d_exp_wins"]):
            print(f"  {s['team']:<16} {s['exp_wins']:>8.2f} {s['d_exp_wins']:>+7.2f} "
                  f"{s['played']:>6} {s['moved']:>6}")

        detail = [(l, s) for l, s in results if s["moved"] or s["newly_played"]]
        if detail:
            for lines, _ in detail:
                print()
                print("\n".join(lines))
        else:
            print("\n  No game was newly played and no forecast moved.")

    if missing:
        print(f"\n  NO CAPTURES ON FILE: {', '.join(missing)}")
    if written:
        print(f"\n  archived {len(written)} report(s) -> {written[0].parent}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Skill mechanics

The skill-specific branch of [`writing-for-agents`](SKILL.md): what changes when the document is a skill (frontmatter, the invocation choice, and router skills). Everything else about writing it is the universal reference in `SKILL.md`.

## Invocation

Two choices, trading the two loads:

- A **model-invoked** skill keeps a `description`, so the agent can fire it autonomously, and other skills can reach it. You can still type its name: model-invocation always _includes_ user reach; a description only ever adds agent discovery, never removes the human's. The description is the skill's top-level context pointer, forced to stay loaded at all times: permanent context load in exchange for discoverability. A model-invoked skill whose content is all reference is also one home for shared reference: another skill can invoke it, so reference needed by several skills lives in one place. Mechanics: omit `disable-model-invocation`, and write a model-facing description carrying the trigger branches (the pointer-writing rules in `SKILL.md` apply in full).
- A **user-invoked** skill strips the description from the agent's reach: only the human typing its name can invoke it, and no other skill can. Zero context load, but it spends cognitive load: you are the index that must remember it exists. Mechanics: set `disable-model-invocation: true`; the `description` becomes human-facing: a one-line summary, trigger lists stripped.

Pick model-invocation only when the agent must reach the skill on its own, or another skill must. If it only ever fires by hand, make it user-invoked and pay no context load.

Shared reference that two user-invoked skills both need can live in neither: with no descriptions, neither can fire the other. Push it to a plain file outside the skill system: external reference any skill can point at.

## Splitting by invocation

The invocation cut of splitting (the sequence cut lives in `SKILL.md`): split off a model-invoked skill when you have a distinct leading word that should trigger it on its own (a trigger word you actually use in your prompts), or another skill must reach it. You pay context load for the new always-loaded description, so that independent reach has to be worth it.

## Router skills

When user-invoked skills multiply past what you can remember, that piled-up cognitive load is cured by a **router skill**: one user-invoked skill that names the others and when to reach for each, so the human has one skill to remember instead of many. It can only hint, never fire them: user-invoked skills have no description, so nothing but the human can reach them.

---
name: forecast-capture
description: >-
  Freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts for all 16 Big 12 teams before
  kickoff, then report what moved since the last capture. Use for "/forecast-capture",
  "capture the forecast", "run the CFB capture", or "did we capture this week". For
  live scores, standings, or schedules, use pp-espn.
---

# Forecast Capture

The report at cfbvictorymodel.com **overwrites each game's Chance of Victory
with the result once the game is played**. That erased every pre-game forecast
from 2019 to 2025. This skill freezes the forecasts once per game week, so 2026
is the first season that can be graded. A forecast exists only until kickoff:
there is no backfill.

Run it on the Mac, from the main checkout `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`, ideally
**Wednesday** of a game week (after the model has taken in the weekend, before
any Thursday game). Thursday or Friday works when no Big 12 game has kicked off
yet. Takes no arguments.

## Steps

1. **Find the last capture.**
   `ls ~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/ | tail -1`
   A gap of 8+ days *may* mean a lost week. A week is lost only if a Big 12
   game was played inside the gap with no capture before it; check that before
   calling it lost (step 2's scoreboard, one date at a time).

2. **Check nothing this week has kicked off.** For each day from Thursday of
   this week through today:
   `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`
   (`groups=4` is the Big 12; a date range returns nothing.) Any game whose
   `status.type.name` is not `STATUS_SCHEDULED` has lost its pre-game
   forecast: name it in the report.

3. **Run the wrapper.** It is the one route; read it for what it runs.
   `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`
   It captures all 16 teams, compares with the last capture, archives both to
   `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`, then prints model vs opening line.
   A Chrome window opens: the capture runs headed by design, because headless
   Power BI never renders most of the team list. Budget ~10 minutes.
   `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is normal start-up racing.

4. **Read the capture result.** Success is exit 0 and no `FAILED for:` line.
   On failure the wrapper prints `comparison SKIPPED` and compares nothing.
   Fix the cause and re-run the failed teams only:
   `scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams <failed teams>`. Re-running the same day is
   safe: it replaces that day's snapshot and log rows. Error fixes are in
   [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md).

5. **Check the report link is live.** After a game weekend, the comparison
   must show games newly played. If it prints
   `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.`, treat it as a **dead
   report link**, not a quiet week: the site swapped its Power BI report around
   10-05, the old link kept loading frozen data with no error, and weeks 6-7
   were lost that way. Open https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/
   in a browser, compare the iframe's `view?r=` key with `REPORT` in
   `weekly_capture.py`, update `REPORT` if they differ, and re-run step 3.
   (Plain `curl` of that page returned HTTP 406 on 2026-10-31.)

6. **Report back**, short. Lead with how many of 16 teams captured, then the
   rollup table (team, exp wins, change, played, moved). Then:
   1. **Games played since last capture**: side correct/wrong and margin miss,
      from each team's `GAMES PLAYED SINCE LAST CAPTURE` block. This track
      record is the point of the whole project.
   2. **Forecasts that moved**: which games and by how much. A big swing
      usually means the model re-rated an opponent after its weekend.
   3. **Season outlook drift**: expected wins now vs last capture.
   4. **Model vs opening line**: name every `CHECK` game (15+ point gap; the
      line was the better 2026 forecast, `docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md`).
      If the wrapper printed `CFBD line pull failed`, say the table is missing.
   5. **Anomalies and losses**: a game appearing or vanishing, fewer than 12
      games for a team, a wild swing, and any lost week or game from steps 1-2.

**Done when** the wrapper exited 0 with 16 snapshots dated today, step 5 showed
games newly played (or `REPORT` was fixed and the capture re-run), and the
report covers all five items, with every lost game named.

## Scope

All 16 Big 12 teams, every week. The list has one home: `BIG12` in
`weekly_capture.py`; edit it there if the conference changes. One full run per
game week keeps load light on a one-person hobby server; teams outside the Big
12 are added only on request (see [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md)).

# Forecast Capture: reference

Read the section that matches what went wrong.

## Errors and fixes

- **`Executable doesn't exist at .../chromium-<N>/...`**: the wrapper's
  `uv run --with playwright` took a newer playwright that wants its own browser
  build. Install it, then re-run (about 95 MB):
  `uv run --with playwright python -m playwright install chromium`
  (from `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`). Seen 2026-09-23.
- **`ModuleNotFoundError: playwright`**: someone ran `python3 weekly_capture.py`
  directly. No Python on the Mac has playwright installed; run the wrapper, or
  `uv run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py ...`. Never fixed by
  reinstalling browsers.
- **`<Team>: '<name>' never appeared (saw [...])`**: the name does not match
  the report's Team slicer. The list shows up to six names the slicer offered
  for that search; copy the exact spelling ("Iowa State", "UCF").
- **`search box never appeared`**: the report's UI changed; the slicer code in
  `weekly_capture.py` needs updating.
- **Archive copies land in the wrong folder**: the run came from a git
  worktree. `ARCHIVE = ROOT.parent / "CFB_Forecast_Archive"` resolves inside
  `.claude/worktrees/`. Run from the main checkout.

## Teams outside the Big 12

Only when Eric asks; each team is another slow slicer pass on the server.

`scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams Baylor TCU "Texas Tech"`

`--team X` takes one team; `--year 2027` another season (the model-vs-line step
still reads 2026 CFBD files; see the shortcut note in `market_view.py`).

## Running unattended

It cannot. The capture needs a headed Chrome in a logged-in macOS session, so
`~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh forecast-capture` still opens a window, and
it is not a launchd job. Nothing nags in season: the morning cadence job only
logs DUE/OVERDUE to `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log`.

## Where things are

Canonical data is `data/weekly_snapshots/<date>_<team>.csv` and the
append-only `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` in the repo.
`~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/` is a read-only mirror (snapshots plus
`<date>_<team>_compare.txt`); read from the repo, not the mirror.

---

# Forecast Capture

The report at cfbvictorymodel.com **overwrites each game's Chance of Victory
with the result once the game is played**. That erased every pre-game forecast
from 2019 to 2025. This skill freezes the forecasts once per game week, so 2026
is the first season that can be graded. A forecast exists only until kickoff:
there is no backfill.

Run it on the Mac, from the main checkout `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`, ideally
**Wednesday** of a game week (after the model has taken in the weekend, before
any Thursday game). Thursday or Friday works when no Big 12 game has kicked off
yet. Takes no arguments.

## Steps

1. **Find the last capture.**
   `ls ~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/ | tail -1`
   A gap of 8+ days *may* mean a lost week. A week is lost only if a Big 12
   game was played inside the gap with no capture before it; check that before
   calling it lost (step 2's scoreboard, one date at a time).

2. **Check nothing this week has kicked off.** For each day from Thursday of
   this week through today:
   `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`
   (`groups=4` is the Big 12; a date range returns nothing.) Any game whose
   `status.type.name` is not `STATUS_SCHEDULED` has lost its pre-game
   forecast: name it in the report.

3. **Run the wrapper.** It is the one route; read it for what it runs.
   `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`
   It captures all 16 teams, compares with the last capture, archives both to
   `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`, then prints model vs opening line.
   A Chrome window opens: the capture runs headed by design, because headless
   Power BI never renders most of the team list. Budget ~10 minutes.
   `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is normal start-up racing.

4. **Read the capture result.** Success is exit 0 and no `FAILED for:` line.
   On failure the wrapper prints `comparison SKIPPED` and compares nothing.
   Fix the cause and re-run the failed teams only:
   `scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams <failed teams>`. Re-running the same day is
   safe: it replaces that day's snapshot and log rows. Error fixes are in
   [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md).

5. **Check the report link is live.** After a game weekend, the comparison
   must show games newly played. If it prints
   `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.`, treat it as a **dead
   report link**, not a quiet week: the site swapped its Power BI report around
   10-05, the old link kept loading frozen data with no error, and weeks 6-7
   were lost that way. Open https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/
   in a browser, compare the iframe's `view?r=` key with `REPORT` in
   `weekly_capture.py`, update `REPORT` if they differ, and re-run step 3.
   (Plain `curl` of that page returned HTTP 406 on 2026-10-31.)

6. **Report back**, short. Lead with how many of 16 teams captured, then the
   rollup table (team, exp wins, change, played, moved). Then:
   1. **Games played since last capture**: side correct/wrong and margin miss,
      from each team's `GAMES PLAYED SINCE LAST CAPTURE` block. This track
      record is the point of the whole project.
   2. **Forecasts that moved**: which games and by how much. A big swing
      usually means the model re-rated an opponent after its weekend.
   3. **Season outlook drift**: expected wins now vs last capture.
   4. **Model vs opening line**: name every `CHECK` game (15+ point gap; the
      line was the better 2026 forecast, `docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md`).
      If the wrapper printed `CFBD line pull failed`, say the table is missing.
   5. **Anomalies and losses**: a game appearing or vanishing, fewer than 12
      games for a team, a wild swing, and any lost week or game from steps 1-2.

**Done when** the wrapper exited 0 with 16 snapshots dated today, step 5 showed
games newly played (or `REPORT` was fixed and the capture re-run), and the
report covers all five items, with every lost game named.

## Scope

All 16 Big 12 teams, every week. The list has one home: `BIG12` in
`weekly_capture.py`; edit it there if the conference changes. One full run per
game week keeps load light on a one-person hobby server; teams outside the Big
12 are added only on request (see [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md)).

# Forecast Capture

Freezes cfbvictorymodel.com's forecasts for the coming weekend, then reports
what changed. Takes no arguments and asks nothing — all 16 Big 12 teams and
2026 are the defaults and rarely change.

## Why this exists

The report's "Chance of Victory" column is **overwritten with the realised
result** once a game is played. Across 2019–2025 that destroyed every pre-game
probability the model ever produced. Miss a week and that week's forecast is
gone permanently — it cannot be recovered later. This makes 2026 the first
gradable season.

## Run it

One command does everything — capture all 16 Big 12 teams, compare, and copy
both into the archive:

```bash
/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh
```

That wrapper is the only route to run. It hardcodes the absolute `uv` path
(`/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv`) so it works from any shell, and it calls:

```bash
uv run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py            # default = all Big 12
uv run python compare_snapshots.py --all --archive
```

Pass through to narrow it — `scripts/weekly_run.sh --team Baylor` for one team,
`--year 2027` for another season.

Snapshots are written to `data/weekly_snapshots/` (canonical) and copied to
`~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/` together with each team's comparison
text. The archive is a read-only mirror; never treat it as the source.

Then read the comparison output back to the user in plain language (see below).

**Budget ~10 minutes.** Sixteen teams share one report session. This is a
hobby server run by one person — do not run it more often than weekly, and do
not add teams beyond the conference without a reason.

**Must run headed.** A Chrome window will open — that is expected, not a bug.
In headless mode Power BI's virtualised slicer list never renders past the
first ~8 alphabetical teams and most teams are unreachable. Do not add
`--headless`.

`Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` in the output is **normal** — the first
slicer interaction races the app's own start-up. It retries 3×, and any team
still failing gets one whole extra pass at the end. Only treat it as a failure
if a team appears in the final `FAILED for:` line.

## What to report back

Lead with how many of the 16 teams captured, then give the rollup table
`compare_snapshots.py --all` prints (team, expected wins, change, played,
moved). Then:

1. **Games played since last capture** — the forecast is now gradable for
   those. Report side correct/wrong and margin miss. This is the accumulating
   track record; it is the whole point.
2. **Forecasts that moved** — which games and by how much. A big win-probability
   swing usually means the model re-rated an opponent after their weekend.
3. **Season outlook drift** — expected wins now vs last week.
4. **Model vs opening line** — the table `market_view.py` prints at the end of the
   run. Name any `CHECK` game: the two disagree by 15+ points, and the line was
   the better 2026 forecast (`docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md`).
5. **Anything anomalous** — a new game appearing, a game vanishing, fewer than
   12 rows, or a wild swing worth a second look.

## Timing

Run **Wednesday** of a game week. Wednesday sits after the model has ingested
the previous weekend and safely before Thursday-night kickoffs. Monday risks
catching the model mid-update; Friday risks missing a Thursday game.

user which week was missed — that forecast is unrecoverable and the gap should
be recorded rather than quietly ignored.

## Which machine

**The Mac owns the weekly capture (decided 2026-09-23).** On Windows, do not run
it — stop and tell the user. On 9/23 both machines captured Baylor, and the sync
merge conflicted on `data/weekly_forecast_log.csv` and that day's snapshot.

The default is the whole Big 12 — all 16, every week. The list lives in one
place, `BIG12` in `weekly_capture.py`. Edit that constant if the conference

  playwright` fetches it per-run (~12ms, cached). Never remove `--with playwright` from

---
name: forecast-capture
description: >-
  Freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts for all 16 Big 12 teams before
  kickoff, then report what moved since the last capture. Use for "/forecast-capture",
  "capture the CFB forecast", or "did we capture this week". For live scores,
  standings, or schedules, use pp-espn.
---

# Forecast Capture

The report at cfbvictorymodel.com **overwrites each game's Chance of Victory
with the result once the game is played**. That erased every pre-game forecast
from 2019 to 2025. This skill freezes the forecasts once per game week, so 2026
is the first season that can be graded. A forecast exists only until kickoff:
there is no backfill.

Run it on the Mac, from the main checkout `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`, ideally
**Wednesday** of a game week (after the model has taken in the weekend, before
any Thursday game). Thursday or Friday works while no Big 12 game has kicked off.
Takes no arguments.

## Steps

1. **Find the last capture.**
   `ls ~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/ | tail -1`
   A gap of 8+ days *may* mean a lost week. A week is lost only if a Big 12
   game was played inside the gap with no capture before it; confirm with
   step 2's scoreboard query on the gap's game days before calling it lost.

2. **Check nothing this week has kicked off.** For each day from Thursday of
   this game week through today:
   `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`
   (`groups=4` is the Big 12; one date per call, a range returns nothing.) A
   game whose `status.type.name` is anything but `STATUS_SCHEDULED` has lost
   its pre-game forecast: name it in the report.

3. **Run the wrapper.** It is the one route; read it for what it runs.
   `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`
   It captures all 16 teams, compares with the last capture, archives both to
   `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`, then prints model vs opening line.
   A Chrome window opens: the capture runs headed by design, because headless
   Power BI never renders most of the team list. Budget ~10 minutes.
   `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is normal start-up racing.

4. **Read the capture result.** Success is exit 0 and no `FAILED for:` line.
   On failure the wrapper prints `comparison SKIPPED` and compares nothing.
   Fix the cause and re-run the failed teams only:
   `scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams <failed teams>`. Re-running the same day is
   safe: it replaces that day's snapshot and log rows. Error fixes are in
   [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md).

5. **Check the report link is live.** After a game weekend, the comparison
   must show games newly played. If it prints
   `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.` (one team:
   `No material change`), treat it as a **dead report link**, not a quiet
   week: the site swapped its Power BI report around 10-05, the old link kept
   loading frozen data with no error, and weeks 6-7 were lost that way. Open
   https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ in a browser, compare
   the iframe's `view?r=` key with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`, update
   `REPORT` if they differ, and re-run step 3. (Plain `curl` of that page got
   HTTP 406 on 2026-10-31.)

6. **Report back**, short. Lead with how many of 16 teams captured, then the
   rollup table (team, exp wins, change, played, moved). Then:
   1. **Games played since last capture**: side correct/wrong and margin miss,
      from each team's `GAMES PLAYED SINCE LAST CAPTURE` block. This track
      record is the point of the whole project.
   2. **Forecasts that moved**: which games and by how much. A big swing
      usually means the model re-rated an opponent after its weekend.
   3. **Season outlook drift**: expected wins now vs last capture.
   4. **Model vs opening line**: name every `CHECK` game (15+ point gap; the
      line was the better 2026 forecast, `docs/MODEL_AUDIT_2026-10-30.md`).
      If the wrapper printed `CFBD line pull failed`, say the table is missing.
   5. **Anomalies and losses**: a game appearing or vanishing, fewer than 12
      games for a team, a wild swing, and every lost week or game from steps 1-2.

**Done when** the wrapper exited 0 with 16 snapshots dated today, step 5 showed
games newly played (or `REPORT` was fixed and the capture re-run), and the
report covers all five items, with every lost game named.

## Scope

All 16 Big 12 teams, every week. The list has one home: `BIG12` in
`weekly_capture.py`; edit it there if the conference changes. One full run per
game week keeps the load light on a one-person hobby server; teams outside the
Big 12 only on request (see [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md)).

2. **High — [SKILL.md:78](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:78)**  
   The done check requires newly played games. That cannot work when there was no game since the last capture, or when a team has no prior capture. A quiet comparison also does not prove the link is dead.

3. **High — [SKILL.md:25](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:25)**  
   The command finds the latest file for any team. It can hide missed captures for other teams. A game after that date may already have a valid forecast, so its status alone cannot prove a loss. Check each team and game against its last capture.

4. **High — [SKILL.md:46](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:46)**  
   On a partial failure, the capture already writes and archives successful teams. The wrapper says nothing was archived, but that is not correct. A later error can also stop the wrapper without the `comparison SKIPPED` message.

5. **Medium — [SKILL.md:54](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:54)**  
   `No material change` is printed for each quiet team in its own report. It does not mean the whole report link is dead. The retry message can also have causes other than normal startup.

6. **Medium — [SKILL.md:75](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:75)**  
   The comparison script reports new games, but it does not report games that vanished. The skill must direct a separate check for missing games.

7. **Medium — [SKILL.md:72](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/SKILL.md:72)**  
   The line pull can succeed while `market_view.py` fails. In that case the wrapper prints `market view failed` and still exits successfully. The skill only tells the reader to check for `CFBD line pull failed`.

8. **Low — [REFERENCE.md:16](/Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/REFERENCE.md:16)**  
   The error starts with the slicer name, such as `Team:`, not the team name. A missing option can also result from a slow or failed page, so it does not prove the spelling is wrong.

The other checked message fragments match the scripts. The `weekly_capture.py` change keeps the same team values and order. It does change the list from a separate copy to the same list object, but the script does not change that list, so normal capture behavior stays the same.

I did not run the capture or write any files.

---
name: forecast-capture
description: >-
  Freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts for all 16 Big 12 teams before
  kickoff, then report what moved since the last capture. Use for "/forecast-capture",
  "capture the CFB forecast", or "did we capture this week". Do not use for live
  scores, standings, or schedules (use pp-espn).
---

# Forecast Capture

The report at cfbvictorymodel.com **overwrites each game's Chance of Victory
with the result once the game is played**. That erased every pre-game forecast
from 2019 to 2025. This skill freezes the forecasts once per game week, so 2026
is the first season that can be graded. A forecast exists only until kickoff:
there is no backfill.

Run it on the Mac, from the main checkout `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model`, ideally
**Wednesday** of a game week (after the model has taken in the weekend, before
any Thursday game). Thursday or Friday works while no Big 12 game has kicked off.
Takes no arguments.

## Steps

1. **Find the last capture.**
   `ls ~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/data/weekly_snapshots/ | tail -16`
   All 16 should share the newest date; a team missing from it failed last
   time and its gap runs from its own newest file. A gap of 8+ days *may* mean a lost week. A week is lost only if a Big 12
   game was played inside the gap with no capture before it; confirm with
   step 2's scoreboard query on the gap's game days before calling it lost.

2. **Check nothing this week has kicked off.** For each day from Thursday of
   this game week through today:
   `curl -s "https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/college-football/scoreboard?groups=4&dates=YYYYMMDD&limit=100"`
   (`groups=4` is the Big 12; one date per call, a range returns nothing.) A
   game whose `status.type.name` is anything but `STATUS_SCHEDULED` has lost
   its pre-game forecast: name it in the report.

3. **Run the wrapper.** It is the one route; read it for what it runs.
   `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`
   It captures all 16 teams, compares with the last capture, archives both to
   `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`, then prints model vs opening line.
   A Chrome window opens: the capture runs headed by design, because headless
   Power BI never renders most of the team list. Budget ~10 minutes.
   `Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` is normal start-up racing.

4. **Read the capture result.** Success is exit 0 and no `FAILED for:` line.
   On failure the wrapper prints `comparison SKIPPED` and compares nothing.
   Fix the cause and re-run the failed teams only:
   `scripts/weekly_run.sh --teams <failed teams>`. Re-running the same day is
   safe: it replaces that day's snapshot and log rows. Error fixes are in
   [REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md).

5. **Check the report link is live.** After a game weekend, the comparison
   must show games newly played. If it prints
   `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.` (in a single-team run:
   `No material change`), treat it as a **dead report link**, not a quiet
   week: the site swapped its Power BI report around 10-05, the old link kept
   loading frozen data with no error, and weeks 6-7 were lost that way. Open
   https://cfbvictorymodel.com/team-schedule-overview/ in a browser, compare
   the iframe's `view?r=` key with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`, update

## forecast-capture audit: done. Nothing pushed, and no capture was run.

**(a) Real bugs found and fixed**
- The skill said "If nothing moved, say so in one line." That instruction is how the dead report link went unnoticed for three weeks (10-07, 10-14 and 10-23 were frozen copies), and weeks 6-7 were lost. The fix is a new step 5: if the comparison prints `No game was newly played and no forecast moved.` after a game weekend, treat it as a dead report link. Compare the iframe on the site with `REPORT` in `weekly_capture.py`, then fix `REPORT` and re-run.
- The skill said to watch for the comparison's warning that the newest capture is several days old. That warning never prints in a wrapper run, because the capture runs first and its age is always 0. The gap check is now step 1, it checks each team (`ls ... | tail -16`, all 16 should share the newest date), and the old sentence is gone.
- The lost-game check used only Baylor's ESPN schedule (team 239). It now uses the Big 12 scoreboard (`groups=4`, one date per call). It also counts a game that has kicked off as lost only if no capture was made earlier that week before kickoff.
- `weekly_capture.py` had a second copy of the Big 12 team list in `CONFERENCES["Big 12"]`, plus leftover paste notes from the 09-09 merge ("# Paste CONFERENCES here", "# 2. REPLACE ..."). `CONFERENCES["Big 12"]` now points at `BIG12` itself, and the paste notes are deleted. Team values and order are unchanged.
- When a capture fails, `weekly_run.sh` printed "Nothing was compared or archived." That was wrong: teams that succeeded are already saved and archived. The message now says so.
- The skill only checked for `CFBD line pull failed`. It now also covers `market view failed`, which can print while the run still exits 0. It also notes that the comparison never names a game that vanished; a team with fewer than 12 games is the only sign.
- Writing pass: steps in run order, a **Done when** line, and positive wording instead of bans. The run block that copied the wrapper's commands is gone (it was out of date: it missed the market-view step). The dead Windows section is cut. Errors, teams outside the Big 12, running unattended and file locations moved to a new sibling file, `~/.claude/skills/forecast-capture/REFERENCE.md`. It now also covers the worktree trap (archive copies land in the wrong folder).

**(b) Commits**
- skills `0204fad`, `3a81272`, `aecf6d7`
- CFB_Victory_Model `6770e76` (`weekly_capture.py`), `a84cd31` (`scripts/weekly_run.sh`)

**(c) Codex review:** `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-forecast-capture-2026-10-31.md`
- Fixed:
  - #2: the Done line now also passes when the scoreboard shows no Big 12 game since the last capture.
  - #3: the gap check covers each team, and step 2 got the earlier-capture rule.
  - #4: corrected the wrapper's failure message.
  - #5, first half: the `No material change` string is now marked as single-run only.
  - #6: vanished games.
  - #7: `market view failed`.
  - #8: the error text is `Team: '<name>' never appeared` and counts as a wrong name only if it fails on both passes.
- Rejected:
  - #1, check the link before capturing: the only way to check before capturing is a browser, since plain `curl` gets HTTP 406. A same-day re-run after fixing `REPORT` replaces the stale snapshot.
  - #5, second half, the retry message: the second pass already tells a slow page from a wrong name.

**(d) Not tested, and why**
- Not run: `weekly_run.sh` end to end and any capture (the mid-season rule; a Saturday run could write a freeze).
- Not run: `cfbd_pull.py` and `market_view.py`, because the wrapper's line step moves files under `data/cfbd/`.
- Not tested: step 5's browser check (open the site page, compare the iframe key). Plain `curl` of that page returns HTTP 406. A retry with browser-like headers was blocked by the auto-mode classifier as bot-check circumvention, so I did not try again.
- Not tested: the other conferences' team names in `CONFERENCES` against the slicer.
- Tested, all read-only:
  - `--help` for both `weekly_capture.py` and `compare_snapshots.py`.
  - An assert that `CONFERENCES['Big 12'] is BIG12` and the list has 16 teams.
  - `compare_snapshots.py --all` without `--archive`. It shows 16/16 for 10-30, and the column names match the skill.
  - The ESPN Big 12 scoreboard for 11-05 (no games) and 10-31 (6 games, all `STATUS_SCHEDULED` when checked).
  - `bash -n` on the wrapper, and the portability check (42/42 pass).

**(e) Headline:** "Nothing moved → one line" hid the dead report link that lost weeks 6-7. The gap check was Baylor-only and its stale-capture warning never fired.

**(f) For the coordinator (shared files)**
- `~/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/docs/STATUS.md`, Gotchas line 27: the documented `curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" .../team-schedule-overview/ | grep ...` check now gets HTTP 406. The link can only be checked from a real browser. Next item 3 there depends on that curl.
- `~/DEV/COMMANDS.md` A7 (about lines 258-330 and 405-410) has its own copy of the run steps and the 09-02 patch note. That is a second home for facts the skill owns; point it at the skill or trim it.
- Tier A `project_cfb-forecast-capture.md`: could record the 406 and the browser-only link check.
- `SKILL-AUDIT-LIST.md`: Done row for 2026-10-31 with the commits above, then refill Next.
- The chromium-cache and dead-link gotchas are written in both the skill and the repo STATUS. Which file keeps them is your call.
